purpose: Present the complete customer outcome and ordered bounded jobs before executing workflows.
format: English YAML; present the goal to the user in config.language
stage: Plan preflight: a long-running sequence of bounded workflows, not another workflow or product Work node
beforeApproval: Present business, architecture, implementation, UAT, exclusions and the ordered workflow estimate table
Wait for an actual user reply approving the presented plan

sections.business: Customer outcome, actors, autonomous decisions, policies, normal and exception flows; explain change, reuse or non-applicability.
sections.architecture: Service and data owners, call direction, contracts, authorization, Saga/CQRS and recovery impacts at module level.
sections.implementation: Separate backend/frontend changes, repositories, directories, verified existing anchors or proposed new files, quality gates and commit scope.
sections.uat: Named sequential user flows, expected outcomes, evidence and cleanup; distinguish unit/backend E2E from browser UAT.
sections.workflows: Ordered named jobs with purpose, exact Work targets, path/resource ceilings, prior inputs, outputs, criteria and estimated minutes range with assumptions. Estimates are not promises.

approval: A task-creation prompt, original request, assistant message, silence or self-authored receipt never approves a subsequently presented goal. Bind the actual later user reply to the presented scope and goal. Local scripts cannot authenticate a human; preserve real host message provenance.
sequence: Execute listed jobs in order. Pass only accepted typed outputs unchanged. Approval of a plan is not acceptance of future results. Follow existing per-workflow goal and result gates; do not invent approval for future goals with unresolved impacts.
changes: Business, service, authorization, schema, targets or effect-ceiling changes invalidate the affected approval and require a revised user-facing goal.
cleanup: Keep unfinished or failed scope/session drafts for resumption. After all jobs are accepted and canonical Work proof validates, remove only this scope's temporary files and owned sessions. Preserve current product evidence in Work; Git tracks product history. Never recursively delete a shared session root.
legacy: Already running jobs without a presented goal must pause and present their current changes and revised scope; never manufacture retroactive approval.
ownership: Backend owns .starci and canonical .work; frontend resolves them through workspace bindings. Keep .starci local and ignored by Git.

files.index.yaml: Stable Plan ID and relative pointers only; no duplicate execution state.
files.goal/index.yaml: The whole ordered Plan plus exact current workflow goals, their bindings and digests. No history.
files.approval/index.yaml: Pending or actual user decision receipts for each presented goal/result; bind message provenance and hashes. Never infer approval from a task request.
files.run/index.yaml: Current job states, requests, accepted responses, typed handoffs and evidence references. Preserve every completed producer needed by later jobs. No attempt history.

storage: One backend-owned .starci/plans/<plan-id>/ bundle. All workflows in the same Plan share this directory; never create a separate runs tree or a new Plan per workflow.
recovery: Incomplete writes or mismatched Plan digests block resumption; never treat file presence as approval. Keep unfinished bundles. Goal revisions require renewed approval, not overwriting a running goal.
